title: Project: Stall Receipt
story: Chilaka's snack stall needs receipts. Read the item, the price and how many, then print one tidy receipt line.
goal: Read item, price and quantity (three inputs). Print: <item> x<quantity> = <total>
starter:
item = input()
# read the price and the quantity as whole numbers, then print the receipt line
hints: You need three input() calls. Two of them must become whole numbers.
Multiply price by quantity, and put everything into one print using an f-string.

item = input()
price = int(input())
qty = int(input())
print(f"{item} x{qty} = {price * qty}")
socratic: What goes inside the f-string braces?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Project: Stall Receipt”?
solution:
item = input()
price = int(input())
qty = int(input())
print(f"{item} x{qty} = {price * qty}")
alt:
item = input()
price = int(input())
qty = int(input())
total = price * qty
print(item + " x" + str(qty) + " = " + str(total))

clean.label: Finish in 4 lines (use an f-string and skip the extra variable)
